(E)'s p95 is measured in production with an interval. It becomes material if that p95 runs more than 66 ms above today's 184 ms: then no configuration passes every gate and the choice becomes a trade between latency and accuracy.
  • The pick is the best of several candidates. Only if a fresh run reads Brisk-S · Few-shot (12 ex.) (E)'s balanced accuracy more than 0.7 points lower: the one pick out of nine reads high by chance, though today's interval sits wholly above the gate.
  • No arm is the control. Only for claims that one configuration beats another: with no control, each gap is read from the two configurations' own intervals combined as independent, which reads wider than a paired comparison would. The gates read each configuration on its own figures, so the call does not rest on it.

What you could change

What you could changeWhat it decidesWhat happens as it moves
Cell floorWhich configuration survivesRead on point estimates: at a floor at or below 76.7%, Nano-XS · Few-shot (12 ex.) (H) becomes the pick, though its balanced accuracy stays borderline; above 82.9%, no configuration passes; in between the call is Brisk-S · Few-shot (12 ex.) (E).
Balanced-accuracy gateWhether anything passesAbove 90.7% nothing passes; at any lower gate the call stays Brisk-S · Few-shot (12 ex.) (E), since Nano-XS · Few-shot (12 ex.) (H) still misses its cell floor.
Latency budgetHow many configurations passBelow 184 ms nothing passes. A looser budget admits more accurate, costlier configurations, and on cost the call stays Brisk-S · Few-shot (12 ex.) (E).

Method

Cases
48,210 labelled turns per configuration, spread across nine complexity × domain cells; none lost or failed. Repeats are not stated.
Pass
A turn passes when the predicted label matches the gold label. Balanced accuracy is the plain mean of the cells' accuracies, so every cell weighs the same whatever its traffic; it is not the traffic-weighted accuracy in the full tables.
Gates
All three were declared before the run: balanced accuracy at least 90% (declared under the name Overall accuracy, which the charts and tables print), accuracy at least 80% in every cell, p95 latency at most 250 ms. A gate is read on the point estimate; an interval crossing its line marks the option borderline.
Intervals
Cell accuracies carry stated half-widths at the 95% level. Balanced accuracy's interval is derived from its cells: the root of the cells' squared standard errors over their count, the cells read as independent. Gaps between configurations combine each one's own spread as independent, uncorrected for the number of comparisons.
Latency
p95 per configuration on the test setup, with no interval stated.
Cost
Cost per million turns as this run was served; the served model is named for each arm, the provider for none. Monthly figures read the declared volume of 30,000,000 as turns, which the input does not state.
Not compared
No control or production baseline.
Source
Synthetic example data from docs/eval-report-kit/references/r3-classifier.json, run 2026-10-24.
